instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Keep watching for things outside (a stretch of time passing, a drive attached or removed, files someone finished putting in a place, a delivery over the network, a service calling to say something changed, a service's list changing) and tell the person's engine one fact each time, so any tool whose wake hears that kind of fact starts", and give it waiters.
2. The AI calls do_one_thing_in_my_account at @tools with method tools:run, tool tool:notice-when-something-shows-up and its input (the worked example shows one).

3. Read what comes back: Give waiters: the standing orders the noticer keeps (notice-when-something-shows-up.waiter-descriptor rows, each naming one mechanism in do-work/mechanisms, its settings and the kind of fact it emits).

4. To hear a service that calls out (a payment, mail or booking service, or a service that watches many apps for you): give a waiter with mechanism_leaf signed-service-calls.mjs, its `verify` row (which headers hold the signature and timestamp, the signed text, sha256, hex or base64, the replay window: copy it from the service's webhook documentation) and its `shape` row (where the change's kind, id and time sit in the call), credential_name the vault name of the signing secret, and emitted_record change_kind something-changed with payload_fields [where, place, change, at, key, before, after]. Point the service's webhook at the address the waiter listens on. A call not signed as the row says is refused and told to nobody.

5. To hear a service that cannot call out: give a waiter with mechanism_leaf service-lists.mjs, its `request` (the list's url and headers, with {credential} where the key goes), its `shape` (the path of the list, each thing's key, place and time, the next page) and `look_again_seconds`, credential_name the vault name of the key. The first read tells nothing; each later read tells what was added, changed or removed (removed only when list_is_whole).

worked_examples.ask: Keep watching for things outside (a stretch of time passing, a drive attached or removed, files someone finished putting in a place, a delivery over the network) and tell the person's engine one fact each time, so any tool whose wake hears that kind of fact starts

waiters.why: This row IS the clock. Its projection writes the exact clock-tick record at the exact address and path labels clock-ticker wrote, so every trigger rule matching clock-tick keeps firing with no edit.

What timed-action says is due (tools/run-work-later-or-on-a-repeat whenToWake), told as a fact once per occurrence: its settings are timed-action's own rows (schedules; time_windows and actions). A tool hears a schedule with a wake {fact: {kind: due-time, from: [run], match: {schedule_id}}}, a one-off with match {record_id}.

worked_examples.title: Hear when a booking is made, changed or cancelled at a booking service that cannot call out
worked_examples.ask: Tell me whenever someone books, moves or cancels time with me.
worked_examples.given: From tests/service-lists.test.mjs ('the first read tells nothing; the next tells what changed; a refused tell is told again'): a stand-in booking service whose list gains booking 4 between two reads (made-up rows).
worked_examples.hands_back: One fact of kind something-changed with where my-booking-service-key, place booking, change added, at 2026-11-18T22:00:00.000Z, key 4 and after the booking as JSON text; a wake {fact: {kind: something-changed, from: [run], match: {place: booking}}} hears it.
